name: Gustatory pathway
summary: Taste buds on the anterior two-thirds of the tongue signal through the chorda tympani of the facial nerve, those on the posterior third through the glossopharyngeal nerve, and those on the epiglottis and pharynx through the vagus; all these fibers, with cell bodies in the geniculate, petrosal and nodose ganglia, end in the rostral part of the nucleus of the solitary tract. Second-order axons ascend mainly uncrossed in the central tegmental tract to the ventral posteromedial thalamus and then to the gustatory cortex in the frontal operculum and anterior insula, with connections to the orbitofrontal cortex where taste and smell combine into flavour. Loss of taste therefore localizes to the peripheral nerves far more often than to the brain.

origin.note: Taste receptor cells; first-order neurons in the geniculate (VII), petrosal (IX) and nodose (X) ganglia.

neuronChain.cellBody: Ganglion cell of VII, IX or X
neuronChain.synapse: rostral (gustatory) nucleus of the solitary tract
VPM thalamus (parvocellular) via the central tegmental tract, mostly ipsilateral
gustatory cortex in the frontal operculum and anterior insula

waypoints.note: chorda tympani for the anterior tongue
rostral gustatory nucleus in the medulla
anterior insula and frontal operculum: primary gustatory cortex

termination: Primary gustatory cortex in the anterior insula and frontal operculum; orbitofrontal cortex for flavour; hypothalamus and amygdala for appetite and aversion.

lesionEffectsByLevel.level: Chorda tympani / facial nerve proximal to the chorda
lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Loss of taste on the anterior two-thirds of the ipsilateral tongue (with facial palsy in Bell palsy)
Loss of taste on the posterior tongue, rarely noticed
Ipsilateral ageusia with the other lateral medullary signs
Contralateral or bilateral taste disturbance, usually subtle

lesionEffectsByLevel.level: Middle ear surgery or lingual nerve injury
lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Metallic taste or loss on the anterior tongue

pearls: Most 'loss of taste' is loss of smell: test both
Taste loss with a facial palsy puts the lesion above the chorda tympani, in the mastoid segment or higher
